matches.rationale: Ground truth concerns missing statistical significance measures (standard deviations, confidence intervals) for Table 1 FID results. None of the findings identify this specific issue; pred_id 2 and 5 report data inconsistencies between tables but do not address the absence of uncertainty quantification.

Both identify the same contradiction in equation (9): the formula averages over N layers/tokens (sum from n=1 to N) while the text states alignment occurs at only one specific layer (n=4 or n=8). This is the identical method logic inconsistency.

Both identify the Abstract/Introduction claim comparing SiT-L/2 + REG @400K to SiT-XL/2 + REPA @4M as problematic. Ground truth notes the claim oversimplifies model capacity differences; pred_id 4 shows the claim is numerically unsupported by Table 1 (9.8 vs 5.9, not comparable). Same underlying issue of exaggerated cross-model comparison.

Ground truth concerns the general absence of variability measures (standard deviations, multiple runs) across all experimental metrics. No finding explicitly identifies this systematic protocol omission; findings focus on specific numerical inconsistencies rather than missing uncertainty quantification.

Ground truth critiques rhetorical overstatement in the Introduction (e.g., '63× faster convergence' without caveats). No finding addresses the tone or rhetorical presentation; findings focus on numerical data inconsistencies and equation errors.

Ground truth identifies missing ethical discussion (bias, misuse, IRB statements) in the Appendix/Conclusion. None of the findings mention ethical considerations; all findings are technical (equations, data inconsistencies).

Both identify the same issue in Table 2/16 (Table 8 in findings): REG shows worse FID than REPA at early epochs (e.g., 80 epochs: 1.86 vs 1.42) contradicting claims of superior training efficiency. Ground truth notes narrative ignores early underperformance; pred_id 5 shows the claim 'REG matches quality in 80 epochs' is false under one table version.

Ground truth concerns insufficient guidance on hyperparameters β and λ (tuning, sensitivity, ablation gaps). No finding addresses hyperparameter selection protocol; pred_id 8 identifies an equation inconsistency but not the experimental design issue around hyperparameter tuning.
Ground truth identifies REPA-E [21] as a potentially fabricated or non-existent reference in Related Work. None of the findings examine reference validity or citation integrity.

Both identify unexpectedly large FID improvements in Table 6 from entanglement alone without alignment. Ground truth notes DINOv2-B improves FID from 33.0 to 26.67 (19% gain) is suspicious without supervision; pred_id 6 shows the text claims 19.18% reduction but actual delta is only 9.4%, revealing data integrity issues in the same table.

Ground truth critiques the Conclusion's absolute claim that REG 'fully unleashes' discriminative potential as overgeneralized. No finding addresses this rhetorical overstatement in the Conclusion; findings focus on numerical inconsistencies.

Ground truth concerns Section 4.2's characterization of +0.30% parameters and +0.49% latency as 'negligible' despite potentially significant absolute costs at scale. No finding addresses this contextual framing issue; pred_id 11 mentions the 675M vs 677M parameter discrepancy but not the 'negligible' claim interpretation.

Ground truth critiques the Abstract title phrase 'Is Much Easier Than You Think' as sensational/promotional rhetoric. None of the findings examine the title or rhetorical tone; all focus on technical content errors.
